\section{Gaussian Space --- Gaussian Density}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.GaussianDensity
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Gaussian Density: Introduction}
Translated Gaussian densities represent affine Gaussian indicator averages and admit integrable bounds for their first two mean derivatives. These estimates give differentiability, global derivative bounds, and Lipschitz regularity of bounded measurable Gaussian averages.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Gaussian Density: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Affine Gaussian Indicator Density Formula]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_indicator_gaussian_affine}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $c,s\in\mathbb R$ with $s\ne0$. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\mathbf 1_A(c+sy)\,d\gamma(y)=\int_{\mathbb R} q_{c,s^2}(z)\mathbf
1_A(z)\,dz,
\]
where $q_{c,s^2}(z)$ is the Gaussian density with mean $c$ and variance $s^2$, and
$\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian probability measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a Gaussian density in its mean]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For any real numbers $c,z$ and any nonnegative variance $v$, the function of the mean
$m\mapsto p_v(m,z)$ has derivative at $m=c$ equal to $\frac{z-c}{v}p_v(c,z)$, where
$p_v$ is the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$ (with the zero-variance
density taken to be zero).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrable envelope for the first mean derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative_dominated}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $v>0$ and $M\ge 0$, and write $p_v(m,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-m)^2/(2v))$ for the
Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$. There is a Lebesgue-integrable function
$b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every $m,z\in\mathbb R$ with $|m|\le M$,
$\left|\frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)\right|\le b(z)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a bounded Gaussian average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_integral_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative_dominated, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every
$z\in\mathbb R$. For any positive variance $v$ and real $c$, the function
$m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R}p_v(m,z)f(z)\,dz$ has derivative at $m=c$ equal to
$\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{z-c}{v}p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$, where $p_v(m,z)$ is the Gaussian
density with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of the Gaussian mean score]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\difficulty{3}
For any real numbers $c,z$ and any nonnegative variance $v$, the function $m\mapsto
\frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)$ has derivative at $m=c$ equal to
$\left(\frac{(z-c)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(c,z)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density
with mean $m$ and variance $v$ (with the zero-variance density taken to be zero).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrable envelope for the second mean derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_secondMeanDerivative_dominated}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $v>0$ and $M\ge0$, and write $p_v(m,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-m)^2/(2v))$. There is
a Lebesgue-integrable function $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every
$m,z\in\mathbb R$ with $|m|\le M$,
\[\left|\left(\frac{(z-m)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(m,z)\right|\le b(z).\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Second derivative of a bounded Gaussian average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_integral_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative_dominated, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_secondMeanDerivative_dominated, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every
$z\in\mathbb R$. For any positive variance $v$ and real $c$, the function
$m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)f(z)\,dz$ has derivative at $m=c$ equal to
$\int_{\mathbb R}\left(\frac{(z-c)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$, where
$p_v(m,z)$ is the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Centered second Gaussian moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianReal}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every $c\in\mathbb R$ and $v\ge0$, the Gaussian measure $N(c,v)$ on $\mathbb R$
satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}(z-c)^2\,dN(c,v)(z)=v.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian density integral bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_gaussianPDFReal_mul_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $v$ be a nonzero nonnegative real number, let $c\in\mathbb R$, and let $g,b:\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $b$ is integrable with respect to the Gaussian measure of mean
$c$ and variance $v$, and $|g(z)|\le b(z)$ for every $z$. Then \[\left|\int_{\mathbb
R}p_{c,v}(z)g(z)\,dz\right|\le\int_{\mathbb R}b(z)\,dN(c,v)(z),\] where $p_{c,v}$ is the
Gaussian density and $N(c,v)$ is that Gaussian measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian second mean derivative bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_gaussianPDFReal_secondMeanDerivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianReal}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. For a nonzero
nonnegative real number $v$ and any $c\in\mathbb R$, \[\left|\int_{\mathbb
R}\left(\frac{(z-c)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_{c,v}(z)f(z)\,dz\right|\le\frac2v,\] where
$p_{c,v}$ is the density of the Gaussian measure with mean $c$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian mean derivative integral bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_gaussianPDFReal_mul_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianReal}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. For a nonzero variance
parameter $v\ge0$ and any $c\in\mathbb R$, \[\left|\int_{\mathbb
R}\frac{z-c}{v}\,p_{c,v}(z)f(z)\,dz\right|\le 1+\frac1v,\] where $p_{c,v}$ is the
density of the Gaussian measure with mean $c$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lipschitz continuity of the Gaussian mean derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_integral_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_gaussianPDFReal_secondMeanDerivative_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_integral_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$, and let
$v>0$. The function $c\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{z-c}{v}p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$, where
$p_v(c,z)$ is the Gaussian density with mean $c$ and variance $v$, is Lipschitz with
constant $2/v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lipschitz continuity of Gaussian averages in the mean]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_integral_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_integral_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$, and let
$v>0$. The function $c\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R}p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$, where $p_v(c,z)$ is the
density of a Gaussian with mean $c$ and variance $v$, is Lipschitz with constant
$1+1/v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Differentiability of a Gaussian average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.contDiff_one_integral_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_integral_gaussianPDFReal_mean, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_integral_gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and satisfy $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every
$z\in\mathbb R$. For every variance $v>0$, the function $m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb
R}p_v(m,z)f(z)\,dz$ is continuously differentiable, where $p_v(m,z)$ is the density at
$z$ of the Gaussian distribution with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}
